overview: This file brings together U.S. diplomatic, consular, military, and naval intelligence on Japan’s armed forces and national-defense system during the intensifying mobilization of 1937–1940. Its core is a detailed March 1939 combat estimate covering command, manpower, organization, weapons, aviation, logistics, reserves, naval power, mobilization capacity, doctrine, and strategic position. Supporting documents trace changes among senior commanders, including Hideki Tojo and Seishirō Itagaki; defense-related industrial expansion and controls on foreigners; implementation of the National General Mobilization Law; and the drafting and enactment of sweeping legislation protecting military-resource secrets. Additional reports address Japan’s proposed concentration of military strength on the Asian continent, possible troop discontent in China, expanded recruitment, concealed troop and casualty movements, and an alleged effort to recruit South American pilots.
interest: Shows how U.S. officials assessed Japan's military capability and intentions just before the Pacific War.
